title: Q-Shield protocol benchmark result
description: One measured record per (protocol, mode, suite). Designed so the Week-7 P-CBOM export is a mapping, not a redesign.

suite.description: Group / kex string, e.g. X25519MLKEM768 or mlkem768x25519-sha256

use_cases.description: Which CFDIR use case(s) this track prices, e.g. ["cfdir-3.4"]. Declared per track so the de-duplication rule across overlapping tracks is mechanical rather than editorial: CFDIR's own assumption 8 warns that redundant costs may be counted in different line items and leaves it to the reader to avoid. Once a cost model sums several tracks, double-counting is a live arithmetic risk, so each track states what it prices.

cfdir_framework.description: The CFDIR framework version the use_cases mapping targets, pinned the way a library version is. Their document is dated and states it will be reviewed annually, so a revision is a methodology event rather than a silent change in meaning.

tls_version.description: TLS version of the arm being measured, recorded explicitly rather than left implicit in the suite name. This is the inherent/net boundary drawn through the measurement: CFDIR notes that PQC migration may also require moving from TLS 1.2 to 1.3, and that this uplift is INDEPENDENT of quantum-safe migration. A classical arm on 1.2 would silently bundle that uplift into a figure published as the PQC increment. Both arms are 1.3, deliberately.

phases.description: Layer-A phase decomposition. Keys are phase names; absent for live mode (black-box total).

secret_key_bytes.description: Secret key length in bytes, read from the liboqs binding's own details block. Recorded because storage for larger private keys cannot be priced from public key sizes alone -- qshield-update-spec.md 16.3 makes it blocking for the TCM's Expansion & Retention line item. Absent on suites where the binding does not expose it.

baseline.description: Comparison to the matched classical suite. Null on a baseline record itself.

cross_validation.description: Agreement against canonical references (eBACS/SUPERCOP, liboqs speed tools). See reference_notes for the cycles-vs-nanoseconds caveat.

auth.description: Signature/auth track. First-class because it serves both PQ-cert handshakes and the blockchain framing (signature size + verify speed).

build_path.description: AVX2 / AVX512 / NEON / reference. Confirming the actual liboqs code path is a documented manual step.

cpu_flags.description: Detected SIMD flags as a proxy for build_path

cpu_hz_nominal.description: Approximate; turbo/scaling/steal make absolute cycle conversion unreliable

steal_time_pct.description: CPU steal during the run. Non-zero sustained steal on a burstable instance means the timings were taken while the hypervisor was taking cycles away. Published rather than smoothed.

ec2_instance_type.description: Instance type this record was measured on. Recorded because two hosts can share an architecture: without it, results from different machines collapse into one bucket and a hardware change becomes invisible. See web/lib/data/hosts.ts.

resources.description: Per-operation resource accounting, sampled around the timed loop rather than inside it -- sampling per iteration would perturb the timings the loop exists to collect. qshield-update-spec.md section 15, Tier 1.

measured.description: False where the POSIX resource module is unavailable. The measurement host is Linux; this is only false in local development.

cpu_us_per_op.description: User+system CPU across the loop divided by iterations. On a single-core-pinned harness with nothing else scheduled this reads close to wall time BY CONSTRUCTION; it becomes informative only under contention, which this harness deliberately does not create. Read it as a sanity check, not a finding.

max_rss_delta_bytes.description: Growth in the process resident high-water mark across the loop. NOT a per-operation footprint: ru_maxrss is a peak that never falls, so it is deliberately not divided by the iteration count.

timing_stats.description: Microseconds. Same shape as benchmark.py compute_stats so protocol results slot into the existing pipeline.

ci95_low_us.description: Lower bound of a 95% confidence interval on the MEAN (normal approximation, z=1.96). Null when fewer than two samples. Not a prediction interval for a single operation.

ci95_high_us.description: Upper bound of the same interval.

std_error_us.description: stdev_us / sqrt(n). The quantity the interval is built from. Published alongside stdev_us because the two are routinely confused: stdev describes how far individual samples scattered, this describes how precisely the mean is known.
